latin.426: Quarto, fac esse aliquem Regem ea potentia praeditum, ut possit subditis suis, si velit, animum rebellionis & inobedientiae immittere, putasne eum si sapiens, si justus, si bonus sit, ita fore comparatum, ut iis qui alioqui in urbe illa fideles essent, primum imputet rebellium crimen, deinde ut illud puniat eos privet justitia & fidelitate, ac caeteris virtutibus, ut deinceps non possint non esse ipsi rebelles & scelesti?
latin.427: Noli igitur, quaeso, frater in Christo dilectissime, tales de Deo cogitationes fovere, quae mihi quidem certe horrorem incutiunt. Quinto denique, succurrant nobis Apostoli verba ad Gal. 6. 5. Unusquisque suum onus portabit. Et ad Rom. 14. 12. Unusquisque nostrum de seipso rationem reddet Deo.
latin.428: Putasne in illa die nobis omnibus & singulis reddendam esse rationem de peccato actuali Adami? Nonne nobis singulis sua cuique attributa sunt a Deo voluntates, facultates, actiones, dotes? De his quidem certe reddenda erit ratio singulis nobis, de Adami actione aliquot annorum millibus antequam esse inciperemus perpetrato non erit nobis, sed ipsi Adamo reddenda apud Deum ratio.
latin.429: Caeterum extrema huius tuae comparationis, necnon capitis, si bene intelligantur, verba mihi probantur, haec rebellio capitis qua totam naturam pervasit, tribuitur & imputatur omnibus hominibus.
latin.430: Nempe, rebellio actualis Adami suum ipsa per se naturali efficientia semen, virus, in omnes Adami facultates insevit, atque medullitus infixit, idque malum serpsit, & per generationem naturalem se diffudit, & propagavit, & contagione sua posteros omnes infecit. Itaque, cum sit in singulis hominibus, merito iis tribuitur & imputatur.

pass_a.426: Fourth: suppose a king so powerful he could inject into his subjects, if he wished, a spirit of rebellion and disobedience—would a wise, just, good king first impute the rebels' crime to those otherwise faithful in that city, then punish it by stripping them of justice, fidelity, and the other virtues so they thereafter could not but be rebels and criminals themselves?
pass_a.427: So Placeus begs his dearest brother in Christ not to foster such thoughts of God—they strike him with horror. Fifth and last: the Apostle helps—Gal. 6:5 Each will bear his own burden; Rom. 14:12 Each of us will give account of himself to God.
pass_a.428: Do you think that day we all and each must give account for Adam's actual sin? Has not God given each of us our own wills, faculties, actions, gifts? Of these we each must certainly give account; of Adam's deed done thousands of years before we began to exist, account is owed not by us but by Adam himself before God.
pass_a.429: For the rest, the closing words of this comparison—and of the chapter—if rightly understood, Placeus approves: this rebellion of the head that pervaded the whole nature is attributed and imputed to all men.
pass_a.430: Namely Adam's actual rebellion by its own natural efficiency sowed seed and virus into all Adam's faculties and fixed it to the marrow; that evil crept, spread and propagated by natural generation, and by contagion infected all posterity. So since it is in each human being, it is rightly attributed and imputed to them. Tip: Cap. VII ends; next Cap. VIII opens OT arguments for imputing Adam's actual sin.

426: Fourth, suppose there is some King endowed with such power that he can, if he wishes, inject into his subjects a spirit of rebellion and disobedience. Do you think that if he is wise, if just, if good, he would be so disposed that to those who would otherwise be faithful in that city he would first impute the crime of rebels, then, to punish it, strip them of justice and fidelity and the other virtues, so that thereafter they could not but be themselves rebels and criminals?
427: Do not, then, I beg you, dearest brother in Christ, foster such thoughts about God, which to me at least certainly strike horror. Fifth and finally, let the Apostle's words to Gal. 6:5 help us: Each will bear his own burden. And to Rom. 14:12: Each of us will give account of himself to God.
428: Do you think that on that day account must be rendered by all and each of us for Adam's actual sin? Have not wills, faculties, actions, and gifts been attributed by God to each of us as our own? Of these indeed account will certainly have to be rendered by each of us; of Adam's action, perpetrated some thousands of years before we began to exist, account will not be owed by us, but by Adam himself before God.
429: For the rest, the extreme words of this comparison of yours, and of the chapter, if they are well understood, I approve: this rebellion of the head by which it pervaded the whole nature is attributed and imputed to all men.
430: Namely, Adam's actual rebellion itself by natural efficiency sowed its own seed and virus into all Adam's faculties and fixed it deep in the marrow, and that evil crept, and by natural generation spread and propagated itself, and by its contagion infected all posterity. Therefore, since it is in each human being, it is deservedly attributed and imputed to them.
